version.changelog: verify_ssl:false no longer needs an undeclared urllib3 (removed: httpx never used it); a 404 on login no longer tells you to run the call that just failed; doctor reads the config the tools read.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed read-only VMware Log Insight connector, with expected local credential handling and audit logging.

dimensions.detail: Network access is proportionate to the purpose: the inspected package authenticates to the configured Log Insight appliance, then uses GET endpoints for logs, fields, version, and alerts. POST is used for session creation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv to install the vmware-log-insight package and requires Bash plus local config files. The published package metadata and inspected wheel matched the stated read-only CLI/MCP purpose, but managed environments may still want normal package provenance controls.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to VMware/vSphere/ESXi log investigation, route other VMware tasks to other skills, and advise bounded time windows and limits for searches.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cron, autostart, background worker, or remote persistence was found. The skill does keep disclosed local state: config and .env files, first-load b64 obfuscation/chmod of password variables, and local SQLite audit records that can include tool parameters and results.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose and capability align: it searches and aggregates VMware Log Insight logs and reads alert metadata. These logs can be sensitive, but the artifacts consistently describe a read-only tool surface with no ingest, edit, or delete functions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only where the operator is allowed to query VMware logs. Use a read-only Log Insight service account, keep TLS verification enabled except for controlled labs, protect ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env or inject secrets from a secret manager, and remember that local audit records may retain queried log content.
llm.findings:
[PE2] expected: The flagged chmod 600 references are credential-file permission hardening for ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env, not sudo/root execution or privilege escalation.
[PE3] expected: The .env credential path is disclosed and purpose-aligned for authenticating to the user's configured Log Insight appliance; the docs also recommend secret-manager injection for stronger at-rest secrecy.
[RA2] expected: The flagged local config, .env, and audit database are disclosed local operational state; I found no hidden session persistence, startup mechanism, or autonomous background execution.
